title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency
authors: Jegadeesh, N., & Titman, S.
source: Journal of Finance (original paywalled); accessible via University of Houston mirror
note: The foundational cross-sectional momentum paper. Original 1993 Journal of Finance publication is paywalled; a stable university mirror provides the full text.

title: Time Series Momentum
authors: Moskowitz, T. J., Ooi, Y. H., & Pedersen, L. H.
note: The single most-cited foundational paper on trend-following/time-series momentum. Directly grounds SMA(10/30) crossover.

title: Does the Stock Market Overreact?
authors: De Bondt, W. F. M., & Thaler, R.
source: Journal of Finance -- PAYWALLED, no verified legitimate free copy found
note: The foundational overreaction/reversal paper. Cited by finding and title only -- the only accessible copy found was an unverified mirror site, not used per this project's source-integrity standard.

title: Mean Reversion in Stock Prices: Evidence and Implications
authors: Poterba, J. M., & Summers, L. H.
note: Official NBER PDF, freely available. Second independent source on mean-reversion, alongside De Bondt & Thaler's finding.

title: A Closer Look at the Short-Term Return Reversal
authors: Da, Z., Liu, Q., & Schaumburg, E.
source: Management Science, Vol. 60, Issue 3, pp. 658-674 (DOI: 10.1287/mnsc.2013.1766); open PDF (nd.edu / informs.org)
note: Confirms and extends Jegadeesh's original short-term reversal finding. Third source on mean-reversion for robustness.

title: Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage: Understanding the Low-Volatility Anomaly
authors: Baker, M., Bradley, B., & Wurgler, J.
note: Foundational low-volatility anomaly paper. Grounds the regime classifier's high/low-vol distinction.

title: Betting Against Beta
authors: Frazzini, A., & Pedersen, L. H.
note: Official NBER PDF. Second, independent source on the low-volatility/low-beta effect.

title: The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns
authors: Fama, E. F., & French, K. R.
note: Foundational value/size-factor paper, hosted on a business-school faculty course page (same category of legitimate hosting as NYU Stern/Duke pages already used).

title: Contrarian Investment, Extrapolation, and Risk
authors: Lakonishok, J., Shleifer, A., & Vishny, R. W.
note: Official NBER PDF. Second value-family source.

title: Quality Minus Junk
authors: Asness, C., Frazzini, A., & Pedersen, L. H.
note: Foundational quality-factor paper.

title: The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium
authors: Novy-Marx, R.
source: author's own University of Rochester page
note: Second quality-family source, hosted directly by the author.

title: Capital Market Seasonality: The Case of Stock Returns
authors: Rozeff, M. S., & Kinney, W. R.
source: Journal of Financial Economics (Elsevier) -- PAYWALLED, no free copy found
note: The original January-effect paper. Cited by finding and title only -- genuinely paywalled at Elsevier with no legitimate free copy found.

title: The Halloween Indicator, 'Sell in May and Go Away': Another Puzzle
authors: Bouman, S., & Jacobsen, B.
source: American Economic Review; a PDF link exists via Semantic Scholar, provenance unverified
note: A PDF link was found but could not be independently verified as an authorized copy before ingestion. Confirm manually before placing in data/corpus/raw/.

title: ...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
authors: Harvey, C. R., Liu, Y., & Zhu, H.
note: Foundational paper on multiple-hypothesis-testing corrections in finance. Academic justification for research_stats.multiple_comparisons (Benjamini-Hochberg) already built in Stage 4.

title: Publication Bias in Asset Pricing Research
authors: Chen, A. Y., & Zimmermann, T.
note: The only arXiv-native paper in this batch -- auto-fetchable via the arXiv API. Offers a more moderate counterpoint to Harvey/Liu/Zhu's stricter significance hurdle, giving balanced methodological grounding rather than a one-sided view.

title: A comparative study of the MACD-base trading strategies: evidence from the US stock market
authors: Pat Tong Chio
note: Comparative empirical study of MACD-based trading strategies on US equities. MACD is trend-following/momentum; no existing KNOWN_STRATEGIES rule uses it directly (confirmed by checking backtester/schema.py directly -- only SMA_CROSSOVER, RSI_14_30_70, RSI_2_10_90, and MORNING_STAR exist), so grounds is empty rather than forced onto an unrelated rule.

title: VolTS: A Volatility-based Trading System to forecast Stock Markets Trend using Statistics and Machine Learning
authors: Letteri, I.
note: Volatility-based trading system combining statistics and machine learning. Grounds the regime classifier's volatility-regime distinction, alongside baker_bradley_wurgler_lowvol and frazzini_pedersen_2014.

title: Algorithmic Trading Strategy Development and Optimisation
authors: Owen Nyo Wei Yuan, Victor Tan Jia Xuan, Ong Jun Yao Fabian, & Ryan Tan Jun Wei
note: General algorithmic trading strategy paper combining moving averages, momentum, volatility indicators, and FinBERT sentiment analysis on S&P 500 data (confirmed from the real abstract). Originally proposed as an 'ATR-bucketing' paper -- confirmed real and genuinely on-topic, but the actual abstract does not mention ATR or bucketing specifically. That characterization could not be verified and should NOT be cited as grounding that particular technique; tagged momentum/volatility broadly instead.

title: New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems
authors: Wilder, J. W.
source: Practitioner book (Trend Research); pre-dates open-access norms, no legitimate free copy found
note: The original source introducing RSI -- cited directly as literature_source for RSI_14_30_70 in backtester/schema.py's KNOWN_STRATEGIES (confirmed by reading the code directly, line 215). Its prior absence from this corpus was a real inconsistency between the code and the catalog. Cited by title only; a 1978 practitioner book has no legitimate open-access copy. grounds is rsi_14_30_70 only, not rsi_2_10_90 -- narrower and more accurate than the existing three mean-reversion entries, which ground both, since the code attributes each RSI rule to a different, specific source.

title: Short Term Trading Strategies That Work: A Quantified Guide to Trading Stocks and ETF's
authors: Connors, L. A., & Alvarez, C.
source: Practitioner book (Connors Research); no legitimate free copy found
note: Cited directly as literature_source for RSI_2_10_90, the short-horizon RSI(2) mean-reversion rule, in backtester/schema.py's KNOWN_STRATEGIES (confirmed by reading the code directly, line 227). Its prior absence from this corpus was a real inconsistency between the code and the catalog. Cited by title only; no legitimate open-access copy of this book exists. grounds is rsi_2_10_90 only, not rsi_14_30_70 -- see wilder_1978's own note for why this is deliberately narrower than the existing mean-reversion entries.

title: Seasonality in the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
authors: Heston, S. L., & Sadka, R.
note: The first genuinely accessible primary seasonality source in this corpus (the two existing seasonality entries, rozeff_kinney_1976 and bouman_jacobsen_2002, remain citation-only/unconfirmed). Real, working PDF confirmed by direct download and content inspection (55 pages, same two authors, October 2006 draft). Title/year discrepancy disclosed, not hidden: the originally-proposed source was SSRN abstract_id=687022, titled '...Expected Stock Returns' (2004) -- that specific claimed download link (assets.super.so) returned a real 403 on direct verification. This NYU Stern PDF is titled '...Stock Returns' (no 'Expected'), dated October 2006 -- almost certainly an earlier/differently-titled working draft of the same underlying research by the same two authors (eventually published as Journal of Financial Economics 87 (2008), 418-445), but not a confirmed byte-identical match to the 2004 SSRN listing. grounds is empty: no existing KNOWN_STRATEGIES rule is seasonality-based yet.

title: International Momentum Strategies
authors: Rouwenhorst, K. G.
note: Confirms Jegadeesh & Titman's US momentum finding holds internationally across 12 European countries, 1980-1995. Third momentum-family source, alongside jegadeesh_titman_1993 and moskowitz_ooi_pedersen_2012. Direct PDF confirmed working (200 OK) at Yale's own ICF working-paper archive.

title: Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects
authors: Amihud, Y.
source: Journal of Financial Markets; University of Pennsylvania faculty mirror
note: Introduces the Amihud illiquidity measure -- price impact per dollar of trading volume -- and shows illiquid stocks earn a return premium. Does not fit any of the six hypothesis-family buckets (EffectFamily): it grounds the SCREENER's liquidity metric (data_pipeline.screener's metric='liquidity' option, used to resolve a charter's universe filter), not a hypothesis family a research mandate would investigate. effect_family='liquidity' is therefore a CorpusEffectFamily-only addition, the same pattern as 'methodology' -- see agentic_core/schemas.py's own docstring for why this can't just be added to EffectFamily (it would collide with UniverseFilter.metric's own, different, use of the same word).

title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
authors: Bailey, D. H., & López de Prado, M.
source: Journal of Portfolio Management; author's own site
note: Arguably the most directly relevant methodology paper in this corpus: it is specifically about correcting the Sharpe ratio for selection bias and backtest overfitting under multiple testing -- the exact problem research_stats.multiple_comparisons (Benjamini-Hochberg, already built in Stage 4) solves. Direct PDF confirmed working (200 OK, genuine application/pdf, ~1MB) at the author's own site -- more authoritative than an SSRN mirror.

title: The Relationship Between Return and Market Value of Common Stocks
authors: Banz, R. W.
source: Journal of Financial Economics (Elsevier) -- PAYWALLED, no free copy found
note: The foundational size-effect paper. Genuinely paywalled at Elsevier -- confirmed by independent search, not just taken on claim; only unauthorized mirrors (academia.edu) turned up, not used, same standard already applied to de_bondt_thaler_1985. Cited by finding and title only. effect_family tagged 'value' as the closest fit (no dedicated 'size' bucket exists, and fama_french_1992 -- already in this corpus -- treats size and book-to-market together under the same family) -- this is an inference, not something explicitly specified when this entry was requested, flagged here in case a different categorization was intended. grounds is empty: UniverseFilter has no 'size' screener metric, so nothing yet implements what this paper would ground directly.

title: High Idiosyncratic Volatility and Low Returns: International and Further U.S. Evidence
authors: Ang, A., Hodrick, R. J., Xing, Y., & Zhang, X.
note: Third low-volatility-family source, alongside baker_bradley_wurgler_lowvol and frazzini_pedersen_2014. Official NBER PDF confirmed working (200 OK) and content-verified by direct download (title, authors, and January 2008 working-paper date read from the PDF itself, not assumed). This is specifically the 'International and Further U.S. Evidence' extension, published in the Journal of Financial Economics (2009) -- a distinct, later paper from the same four authors' original 2006 Journal of Finance paper ('The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns', NBER w10852), which was not the one verified or added here. If the original 2006 paper was intended instead, it would need separate verification.

title: Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule
authors: Gatev, E., Goetzmann, W. N., & Rouwenhorst, K. G.
source: NBER Working Paper No. 7032; Wharton mirror
note: Tests pairs trading against bootstrapped random pairs as a control -- methodologically parallel to research_stats' own randomized-entry control (test_significance). Both the official NBER PDF and the Wharton course-page mirror confirmed working (200 OK) independently. grounds is empty: pairs trading (spread mean-reversion between two cointegrated stocks) is a distinct mechanism from any existing KNOWN_STRATEGIES rule -- none currently implement a pairs/spread strategy.

title: The Accrual Anomaly
authors: Dechow, P. M., Khimich, N. V., & Sloan, R. G.
source: SSRN (abstract_id=1793364) -- claimed direct link (assets.super.so) returned a real 403 on verification; no working alternative found
note: A distinct earnings-quality anomaly -- reviews Sloan's own 1996 discovery that firms with high accruals (vs. cash flows) underperform -- separate from the existing profitability-based quality papers (asness_frazzini_pedersen_qmj, novy_marx_2013). Same treatment as banz_1981: real, well-established paper, no verified free copy reachable at this time. A follow-up search for an alternative source mostly surfaced a different, related paper by other authors rather than this specific one.

title: Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap
authors: Sullivan, R., Timmermann, A., & White, H.
source: Journal of Finance -- claimed direct link (kevinsheppard.com) failed with a TLS certificate mismatch on verification; no working alternative found
note: Directly re-tests the technical trading rules of Brock, Lakonishok & LeBaron (1992) using White's Reality Check bootstrap to correct for data-snooping bias -- Brock/Lakonishok/LeBaron (1992) is the exact literature_source already cited for SMA_CROSSOVER (sma_10_30_crossover) in backtester/schema.py's KNOWN_STRATEGIES. Same treatment as banz_1981 and dechow_khimich_sloan_2011: real, well-established paper (Journal of Finance, 1999), no verified free copy reachable at this time -- the claimed source failed a real TLS handshake, not just a broken link, and a follow-up search of UCSD faculty pages (two of the three authors' affiliation) found no working alternative.
